chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Marouf ibn Harrabouz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no servant who is struck by a calamity, so he says the Istirja (Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un) upon remembering the calamity, and he is patient when it strikes him suddenly, except that Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sins; and every time he remembers his calamity and says Istirja upon the remembrance of the calamity, Allah will forgive him every sin he acquired in between.

key_terms.يَسْتَرْجِعُ: He says the Istirja formula (Inna lillahi...)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for saying Istirja when remembering a calamity?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the transformative power of *Istirja* (reciting 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un') not merely as a ritual response, but as a continuous mechanism for spiritual purification. It highlights the concept of cumulative forgiveness, where each mindful remembrance of the calamity serves as a fresh opportunity for Allah to erase sins incurred since the previous instance, thereby turning grief into a means of ascending in spiritual rank.
